subject: Highbridge production latency spike & routing mitigation request
messages:
From: Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@highbridge.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@highbridge.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency surge + 5xx spike — immediate help requested

Sergio,

We're seeing a sustained P95 latency jump to ~2.9s and a 5xx rate climbing to ~6% across our API traffic since ~02:00 UTC. This started right after a large scheduled batch from one of our analytics partners — we can see an unusually high QPS to the embeddings endpoint routed through your us-west-2 AZ2. Our customers are timing out and our payment processing is seeing late retries.

Attached: network traces and a short HAR from the timeout window.

Asking: can you (a) confirm if this is a routing/AZ saturation issue on Redwood's side, and (b) whether you can temporarily redirect our prod traffic to another region (we're ok with us-east-1) while we investigate? This is impacting SLAs.

Thanks — please escalate to whoever owns regional routing.

— Ava Richardson
Head of Platform 
Highbridge Analytics
ava.richardson@highbridge.ai
[attachment: highbridge-network-trace-0305.zip (zip)]
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@highbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge + 5xx spike — immediate help requested

Ava — thanks for the quick flag and the traces. I'm opening a P0 on this and will coordinate a short mitigation plan while we triage.

Quick summary of what I'm seeing so far (preliminary):
- Telemetry shows queueing and elevated CPU on inference hosts in us-west-2 AZ2, correlated with increased long-tail KV cache misses.
- Error profile looks like timeouts / upstream throttles, not application-level model errors.

Proposed immediate mitigation (needs internal approval):
1) Start a controlled geo-swivel: steer 5% of Highbridge prod traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for a 30-minute canary.
2) If the canary is stable, increase diversion to 50% over 15 minutes and monitor 5xx & latency.
3) If diversion improves SLAs, keep diversion in place up to 2 hours while we remediate — not a long-term change.

Impact / risk: cross-region steering increases token egress cost and will change latency profiles for some requests by ~80–120ms. There is a small risk (~1%) of transient failures during the cutover window.

We need explicit ops/exec authorization to perform this out-of-band routing change (this touches routing policies and bypasses normal change freeze). Marcus — can you validate the runbook and confirm rollback steps? Marissa — can you own customer comms if we proceed? Lauren — need your approval to execute emergency geo-steer.

I'll attach a short decision memo in a follow-up.

— Sergio
Director, Technical Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge + 5xx spike — immediate help requested

Sergio / team — quick triage notes from infra:
- Confirmed hotspot on us-west-2 AZ2 inference pool: average CPU at 92%, scheduler backlog growing, connection queue depth spiking.
- KV cache observed high miss rate for a small set of prefixes (likely a hot key pattern from batch retriever).
- No obvious kernel-level network degradation; this looks like contention rather than network partition.

Runbook excerpt (for geo-steer canary):
- Step 0: Create emergency routing policy in control-plane tagged for account HB-2026-EXP-09.
- Step 1: Set steer weight 5% to us-east-1; monitor 5xx and P95 for 10m.
- Step 2: If stable (5xx < 1% and P95 < 1.2s), increase to 50% over 15m.
- Rollback: remove steer policy and force route to origin region.

If we go this path, recommend also throttling the partner job at Highbridge (they indicated it's scheduled) — that will reduce cache churn.

Link to live logs / runbook: https://redwood-console.internal/runbooks/geo-steer-emer/ (internal)

I'll stage the policy and be ready to flip on confirmation.

— Marcus
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge + 5xx spike — immediate help requested

Approved: emergency geo-steer to us-east-1 for Highbridge. Conditions:
- Limit duration to 2 hours unless execs sign off on extension.
- Finance and Sales PM to be notified for cost exception (estimate additional spend ~ $1.4k/hr at 50% diversion).
- Customer comms must be sent within 15 minutes of flip.

Marcus — proceed with the canary when Sergio confirms. Marissa — please prepare the customer-facing note.

— Lauren
VP, Service Operations
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@highbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Actioning: Geo-steer canary started for Highbridge — update & next steps

Ava — quick update and timeline:
- We have approval to start an emergency geo-steer. Marcus has staged the policy.
- At 12:05 PST we will apply a 5% diversion of Highbridge prod traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 (30-minute canary).
- Monitoring: we will watch P95, 5xx, and payment pipeline success rates. If the canary keeps 5xx < 1% and P95 < 1.2s, we'll open to 50% over 15 minutes.
- Expected side-effects: slightly higher round-trip latency for diverted requests (~+100ms) and modest cost bump.

Marissa will send a short customer note confirming the temporary routing and what to expect. We will keep you updated every 15 minutes during the cutover and share a postmortem within 24 hours.

Links: status/public: https://status.highbridge.ai/incident/2027-03-05-01 
Internal runbook: https://redwood-console.internal/runbooks/geo-steer-emer/ 

— Sergio
Director, Technical Accounts
Redwood Inference
